name: Algebra
title: Algebra essentials
intro: Algebra replaces unknown or changing numbers with letters and builds rules for rewriting expressions and solving equations. These lessons go from simplifying expressions through linear equations, inequalities, systems, polynomials, factoring and quadratics. Each lesson stands alone, but earlier arithmetic ideas (fractions, signed numbers, order of operations) are assumed.

lessons.title: Expressions and variables
lessons.summary: Letters for numbers; combining like terms and the distributive property.

sections.p: A variable is a symbol (often x) that stands for a number. An expression combines numbers, variables and operations: 3x + 2. It has no equals sign yet — it is a recipe for a value once x is known.
Substitute the known value and compute with the usual order of operations.
Terms with the same variable part can be combined: 5x + 2x = 7x. Constants combine among themselves: 5x + 3 + 2x − 1 = 7x + 2. You cannot merge 5x and 5 into one term.
a(b + c) = ab + ac. Useful both to expand and (in reverse) to factor out a common factor.

practice.q: Which is an expression (not an equation)?

lessons.title: Solving linear equations
lessons.summary: Isolate the variable with inverse operations.

sections.p: A linear equation in one variable has the form ax + b = c (after simplifying). Solving means finding the number that makes both sides equal.
Do the same operation to both sides: add/subtract the same number, multiply/divide by the same nonzero number. Goal: get x alone on one side.
Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other.
Substitute the answer back into the original equation. Both sides should match.

practice.q: Which step isolates x in x/3 = 6?

lessons.title: Inequalities
lessons.summary: Greater/less than; when multiplying by a negative flips the sign.

sections.p: An inequality compares two expressions with <, >, ≤ or ≥. Solutions are often intervals on the number line, not a single point.
You may add or subtract the same number on both sides. You may multiply or divide by a positive number. If you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.
x > 2 means all numbers larger than 2 (open ray). x ≤ −1 means −1 and everything left of it. Compound: 1 < x ≤ 4 is between 1 and 4, including 4 but not 1.
Open circle for < or >; filled circle for ≤ or ≥. Shade the side that satisfies the inequality.

practice.why: Divide by −2 and flip the inequality.
That reverses order on the number line.
practice.q: When must you flip an inequality?

practice.why: Strict on the left, inclusive on the right.

lessons.title: Linear functions
lessons.summary: Slope-intercept form y = mx + b and graphs of lines.

sections.p: A linear function has constant rate of change. In slope-intercept form, y = mx + b: m is the slope (rise/run), b is the y-intercept (where the line meets the y-axis).
Between two points (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂): m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) when x₂ ≠ x₁. Positive slope rises to the right; negative falls; zero is horizontal.
Plot (0, b), then use slope: from that point, rise and run to the next lattice point. Example: y = 2x − 1 crosses at (0,−1) and goes up 2, right 1.
y = 3 is horizontal (slope 0). x = 2 is vertical (undefined slope) and is not a function of x in the y = f(x) sense.

practice.why: m is the coefficient of x.

lessons.title: Systems of linear equations
lessons.summary: Two equations, two unknowns: graphing, substitution and elimination.

sections.p: A system asks for values that satisfy two (or more) equations at once. Geometrically, two lines may meet at one point (unique solution), be parallel (none) or coincide (infinitely many).
Solve one equation for a variable, plug into the other.
Add or subtract multiples of the equations so one variable cancels.

sections.p: If you reach 0 = 5, the system is inconsistent (parallel lines). If you reach 0 = 0, the equations are dependent (same line).

sections.p: A polynomial in x is a sum of terms aₙxⁿ + … + a₁x + a₀ with nonnegative integer powers. The degree is the highest power with nonzero coefficient. Linear degree 1; quadratic degree 2; cubic degree 3.
Write powers descending: 3x² − 2x + 7, not scattered. Leading coefficient is the one on the highest power.
Combine like terms (same power of x).
Distribute each term of the first across the second (FOIL for two binomials), then combine like terms.

practice.why: Degrees add when multiplying (nonzero leading coeffs).

lessons.title: Factoring
lessons.summary: Greatest common factor, trinomials and difference of squares.

sections.p: Factoring rewrites a polynomial as a product. It undoes expansion and is the main tool for solving many polynomial equations.
Pull out the greatest common factor (GCF) of all terms.
Find integers p, q with p+q = b and p×q = c. Then x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q).
a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).
If AB = 0, then A = 0 or B = 0. So after factoring, set each factor to zero.

lessons.title: Quadratic equations
lessons.summary: ax² + bx + c = 0 via factoring, square roots and the quadratic formula.

sections.p: A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. The graph of y = ax² + bx + c is a parabola; solutions are x-intercepts when they are real.
Factor, then use the zero product property.
If the equation is x² = k with k ≥ 0, then x = ±√k. Complete the square or shift first when needed: (x−1)² = 4 → x−1 = ±2.
For ax² + bx + c = 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a). The discriminant D = b² − 4ac: D>0 two real roots; D=0 one (repeated); D<0 no real roots.

practice.why: Square root of negative is not real.

lessons.title: From words to equations
lessons.summary: Translate phrases into algebra and solve simple models.

sections.p: Word problems become equations when you name the unknown, translate English into operations and write a relation that must hold. Units and a quick check for reasonableness matter as much as the algebra.
“Sum” → +; “difference” → −; “product” → ×; “quotient” → ÷; “is” / “equals” → =; “two more than x” → x+2; “twice x” → 2x; “5 less than x” → x−5 (order matters).
Three consecutive integers summing to 54: n + (n+1) + (n+2) = 54 → 3n + 3 = 54 → n = 17. The integers are 17, 18, 19.
A price after 20% discount is $48. Original p satisfies 0.8p = 48 → p = 60.
